internal_refs.relationship: §859 expressly cross-references §15610.30 — financial abuse as defined there triggers §859 double damages
§859 covers taking by undue influence in bad faith — §15610.70 four-factor test defines undue influence
§859 attorney fees are discretionary BUT §859 explicitly preserves §15657.5 mandatory fees — both apply in financial elder abuse cases

external_refs.relationship: Annual accounting failures = concealment under §859; missed accountings create separate §859 exposure per year
Termination of conservatorship does not extinguish §859 liability for past wrongful property acts
Honeysuckle sale equity shortfall ($356K unaccounted) is subject to §859 doubling if bad-faith disposal proven
Northern Trust / pension trust structures — §859 covers trust property regardless of ERISA preemption analysis of the plan itself; preemption analysis needed

case_law.holding: §859 double damages applied to conservator who wrongfully disposed of conservatee's real property; bad faith established by pattern of concealment in accountings
case_law.significance: Established that accounting concealment satisfies the 'concealed' verb in §859

case_law.holding: §859 double damages apply to decedent estate property wrongfully taken by family member in bad faith; 'value' measured at time of judgment
case_law.significance: Established measure of double damages — value at judgment date, not date of taking
